newsitem.title: USA: CYCLING-HAMPSTEN, FORMER TOUR OF ITALY WINNER, RETIRES.
newsitem.headline: CYCLING-HAMPSTEN, FORMER TOUR OF ITALY WINNER, RETIRES.

text.p: Andy Hampsten, the only American to win the Tour of Italy, announced his retirement Monday after a 12-year career as a professional cyclist.

Hampsten, 34, also twice claimed the Tour of Switzerland, finished as high as fourth overall in the Tour de France, and claimed the pinnacle stage of the sport's prestige event when he won the mountainous ascent to L'Alpe d'Huez in 1992.
"After 12 very rewarding years as a pro, it's time now to concentrate full-time on a lifetime contract with my family," said Hampsten in a prepared statement.

After turning professional in 1985, Hampsten won a stage of the Tour of Italy in 1986 and then joined the famed La Vie Claire team, which included cycling legends Bernard Hinault of France and American Greg LeMond.

Hampsten spent much of his career on the European circuit and rarely competed in his native country until this year when he joined the U.S. Postal Service squad in San Francisco and competed in the Tour DuPont and numerous other U.S. events.
In 1995, Hampsten competed for the famed Spanish team Banesto, captained by five-time Tour de France winner Miguel Indurain.
Earlier this summer, Hampsten finished 33rd overall at the Tour of Switzerland, which he had won twice. He concluded his stage racing career at the Tour of Holland in August.
"If my racing has inspired, motivated or just given a grin to fellow cyclists, I'll be very content," said Hampsten, who now resides in Castagneto Carucci, Italy.
